Start with the expanded examples. Open further examples for options and alternative R approaches.

svy

Survey-weighted logit

Stata 

svy: logit y x

R survey 

survey::svyglm(y ~ x, design = design, family = quasibinomial())

Differs from Stata Match design and missing-data exclusions first; singleton-PSU policy, degrees of freedom and confidence-interval transformations can differ between R and Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

Survey-weighted mean

Stata 

svy: mean x

R srvyr 

summarise(design, x = srvyr::survey_mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))

Differs from Stata Match design and missing-data exclusions first; singleton-PSU policy, degrees of freedom and confidence-interval transformations can differ between R and Stata.

Survey-weighted proportions

Stata 

svy: tabulate x

R srvyr

Differs from Stata Match design and missing-data exclusions first; singleton-PSU policy, degrees of freedom and confidence-interval transformations can differ between R and Stata.

Stata

R srvyr 

design |> group_by(g) |> summarise(x = srvyr::survey_mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))

Differs from Stata Match design and missing-data exclusions first; singleton-PSU policy, degrees of freedom and confidence-interval transformations can differ between R and Stata.

2 more examples and alternatives

Subpopulation estimate

Stata 

svy, subpop(rural): mean x

R srvyr 

design |> filter(rural == 1) |> summarise(x = srvyr::survey_mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))

Differs from Stata Filtering a survey design keeps the full design for the variance, as subpop() does. Match design and missing-data exclusions first; singleton-PSU policy, degrees of freedom and confidence-interval transformations can differ between R and Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

Survey-weighted proportions with intervals

Stata 

svy: proportion x

R srvyr 

design |> group_by(x) |> summarise(p = srvyr::survey_prop(vartype = "ci"))

Differs from Stata Match design and missing-data exclusions first; singleton-PSU policy, degrees of freedom and confidence-interval transformations can differ between R and Stata.

Stata reference · R reference

svyset

Declare a survey design

Stata 

svyset psu [pweight = wt], strata(stratum)

R srvyr 

design <- srvyr::as_survey_design(data, ids = psu, strata = stratum, weights = wt, nest = TRUE)

Differs from Stata Stratified PSU probability-weighted design; nests PSU IDs within strata as Stata does. Inference requires the same sample, singleton-PSU policy and design df.
